answer: To raise the cost of sockpuppet swarms, every identity locks a time-decaying stake and completes a live interactive proof with randomly paired incumbents. The zephyr protocol issues one-shot challenges that expire in seconds, so a factory cannot reuse a scripted reply. Admission depends on a uniqueness delta: cosine distance between the applicant's embeddings and the nearest recent-applicant cluster; below a published threshold, the stake is slashed. Unproven identities stay in a rate-limited reef of low-impact actions until three uncorrelated incumbents countersign them.
